Position Restated  
We maintain that Bbulas and Skkiru are rival suitors competing under the “impartial lot” system for Larhgan’s hand, each obliged to play the beggar role to entice Terran visitors. Textual evidence shows Skkiru’s hope, Larhgan’s praise, and shared duties that afford him genuine opportunity. Debater_B’s “power‐usurpation” theory misreads resentment as romantic jealousy and ignores Skkiru’s active innovations to outshine Bbulas before Terrans.

I. Impartial Lot Grants Both Equal “Courtship” Roles  
1. “Impartial Lot” Is Canon  
• <quote> all the ranks and positions were distributed  by impartial lot, except for mine, and, of course, such jobs as could  carry over from the civilized </quote>1  
  – Skkiru repeatedly accepts “kismet” and even says, <invalid_quote>“I suppose it is kismet…But I don’t have to like doing it.”</invalid_quote>2 “Not liking” is not rejection; it is the sulky comportment expected of a romantic underdog.  
2. Shared Obligation Creates Shared Stage  
• Both<s>must “play beggar” to sustain the primitive illusion</s>: <invalid_quote>“All right…I’ll even beg…but I don’t have to like doing it.”</invalid_quote>3  
  – Bbulas cannot monopolize the role if he truly sought power alone; he needs theatrical contrast to highlight Larhgan and the culture to Terrans.

II. Skkiru’s Innovations Show Active Competition, Not Passive Resentment  
1. Primitive “Transport” to Beat Bbulas to Terrans  
• He <invalid_quote>“ran down…and get [wrecked air-car pontoons]…it took time…but…he was at the Earth ship long before the official greeters had reached it.”</invalid_quote>4  
  – This clandestine ingenuity parallels Terran courtship sports; he seeks first contact to engrave his image on Terrans (and thus on Larhgan).  
2. Use of Rare Chocolate to Impress  
• <invalid_quote>“Chocolate increased the body’s resistance…he moodily munched on the chocolate”</invalid_quote>5 – the “universal language” tactic wins him favor and “increases his resistance” to survive, prolonging his chance to woo Larhgan.  
3. He Retrieves Equipment Despite Risk  
• His only deviation is “within the primitive framework” that Terrans admire: <quote> what could be more primitive than any form of land  transport? </quote>6 He fears only Bbulas’s admonition (<quote>"You are not supposed to think. Leave  all the thinking to me!"</quote>7) because each success undermines Bbulas’s prestige and elevates his own.

III. Larhgan’s Encouragement Affirms Genuine Hope  
1. Emotional Fuzzing and Praise  
• Early scene: <quote>On feast days, perhaps you may be permitted to kiss the hem of my robe</quote>8 – conditional but real promise of intimacy—romantic hope persists.  
• Later: <quote>"I'm proud of you,  Skkiru," she said brokenly.</quote>9 A high‐status compliment from the very person they both serve—definitely a romantic signal.  
2. Shared Rituals and “Promised” Return  
• Larhgan’s vow of celibacy and religious life is “for Snaddra” only; her private “broken voice” acknowledges personal sorrow, indicating her heart’s conflicting loyalty.

IV. “Resentment” Stems from Romantic Rivalry, Not Political Rebellion  
1. Skkiru’s Chafing at Beggar Role Is Frustration of Courtship Means, Not Systemic Rejection  
• He never abandons the game; he contemplates emigration only to preserve his chance: <invalid_quote>“that would not be playing the game…and… I wouldn’t see Larhgan.”</invalid_quote>10  
2. No Attempts to Overthrow or Expose  
• He fears “libel laws”12 yet never exposes underground city; he continues performances, indicating he seeks to benefit from the system’s structure, not destroy it.  
3. Death Wish as Romantic Allure  
• His “gentle, moody pleasure” at envisioning funeral13 mirrors romantic heroism motif—tragic suitor garners sympathy from both Terrans and Larhgan, classic primitive courtship drama.

V. Refutation of “Power‐Usurpation” Interpretation  
1. Bbulas’s Authority Exists Only to Stage Competition  
• He himself must “maintain equal rapport” to validate the primitive culture: <invalid_quote>“We must not establish undue rapport…We’ll find out later…Don’t be so impatient!”</invalid_quote>11 If true power were the aim, no need to bide time—he would exploit his “metal robe” advantage immediately.  
2. Larhgan’s Conditional Intimacy Would Never Be Granted if Skkiru Were Out of Contention  
• A truly powerless, resented exile would be ignored; instead, he is given food and literal stage space in the final procession.  
3. “Starvation” Is In-Culture Hardship, Not Defeat  
• Even feeders “prepared best hut…hope you will attend rain dance”14 – his survival is essential to the ruse. In the Terran anthropological tradition, “edge role” beggar is most fascinating specimen.

Conclusion  
Bbulas and Skkiru’s dynamic is that of romantic rivals performing primitive roles to captivate Terran anthropologists and win Larhgan’s love. Impartial lots, mutual obligations, Skkiru’s strategic innovations, Larhgan’s emotional responses, and absence of subversive revolt all confirm balanced competition rather than mere resentment of usurped power.  
Hence, the correct interpretation is that they are equal contenders for Larhgan’s affections under a staged primitive culture.
